Where it began

Faheem Ashraf was born on 16 January 1994 in Phool Nagar, a town in the Kasur district of Punjab. He grew up in a big household, with two sisters and six brothers, and learned a good deal of his cricket in the tape-ball games that shape so many Pakistani players.

His serious cricket started in 2010 with an inter-district Under-19 competition around Faisalabad. A few seasons later he was playing senior district cricket for Kasur, and in 2013–14 Faisalabad took him into their Quaid-e-Azam Trophy side. He marked his first-class debut that season with a hundred, which is one way to get noticed.

The player

His Test debut came against Ireland in May 2018, and he made 83. A brisk 37 at Lord's followed, then 3 for 60 at Headingley. Between 2018 and 2023 he played 17 Tests, scoring 687 runs at 26.42 with four fifties and a best of 91, made in New Zealand. He also took 25 wickets at 39.64, with 3 for 42 his best.

The white-ball game showed him off too. In 2017 he became the first Pakistan bowler to take a hat-trick in a T20 international, against Sri Lanka in Abu Dhabi. In 2018 he was the leading wicket-taker as Islamabad United won the Pakistan Super League, and the board named him its Emerging Player of the Year.

What made him special

He was never the quickest in Pakistan's attack, and he never pretended to be. What he offered was control: a steady line, a bit of movement off the seam, and spells that kept batsmen quiet while the faster men rested. Captains like a bowler they can throw the ball to without worrying.

With the bat he was a counter-puncher. Several of his best innings, such as an unbeaten 78 against South Africa and that 91 in New Zealand, came after the top order had wobbled. The Test hundred never quite arrived, but four fifties from the lower order is a handy return for a man who was meant to be the extra bowler.

Away from the middle

He became a familiar face in leagues around the world, turning out in Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and for Hobart Hurricanes in Australia's Big Bash. In 2024 he captained Pakistan at the Hong Kong Sixes. In October 2025 he was Player of the Series in a home T20 series against South Africa, taking six wickets, including his best T20 international figures, 4 for 23.

And finally

When the Pakistan Super League held its first auction in February 2026, Islamabad United went back for him and made him the second most expensive signing of the day. Some partnerships are worth keeping.
